name: Louisville Financial Empowerment Center
description: Free one-on-one financial counseling helping Louisville residents improve credit scores, reduce debt, increase savings, and achieve financial goals. Professional financial counselors provide personalized guidance on budgeting, credit repair, and money management.
eligibility: Open to all Louisville residents

name: New Directions Housing Corporation - Financial Literacy
description: Community development organization offering financial education workshops, homebuyer education, credit counseling, and foreclosure prevention. Helping families achieve financial stability and sustainable homeownership.
eligibility: Open to all, focus on low-to-moderate income families

name: Consumer Credit Counseling Service of Louisville
description: Nonprofit credit counseling agency providing debt management plans, budgeting assistance, credit counseling, and bankruptcy counseling. Helping individuals overcome debt and achieve financial wellness.
eligibility: Open to all individuals seeking debt help

name: Kentucky Housing Corporation - Homeownership Programs
description: State housing finance agency offering down payment assistance, affordable mortgage programs, and homeownership education for first-time homebuyers and moderate-income families in Louisville and Kentucky.
eligibility: First-time homebuyers and income-qualified families

name: Dare to Care - SNAP Outreach
description: Food bank offering SNAP (food stamps) application assistance and benefits screening. Helping eligible individuals and families access food assistance and other public benefits to reduce financial strain.
eligibility: Anyone seeking SNAP benefits assistance

name: Metro United Way - 211 Helpline
description: 24/7 helpline connecting people to community resources for food, housing, utilities, healthcare, and more. Simply dial 211 from any phone for free, confidential assistance finding help in the Louisville area.
eligibility: Anyone seeking community resources and assistance

name: La Casita Center
description: Community center serving Louisville's Latino/Latinx families with education, empowerment, advocacy, and wellness programs. Providing ESL classes, citizenship assistance, health education, and community support in a welcoming environment.
eligibility: Open to all, focused on serving Latino/Latinx community

name: Centerstone - Downtown Louisville
description: Mental health and substance abuse treatment center providing comprehensive behavioral health services. Offering therapy, medication management, addiction treatment, and crisis intervention for adults and families.
eligibility: All ages. Most insurance accepted, sliding scale available.

name: Blessings in a Backpack - Louisville
description: Program providing food for elementary school children who may go hungry over weekends. Working with schools throughout Louisville to discretely provide nutritious, kid-friendly food to food-insecure students.
hours: Mon-Fri 9AM-5PM, weekend food distribution through schools
eligibility: Elementary school students identified by school counselors as food insecure

name: House of Ruth - Survivors of Torture Program
description: Specialized services for survivors of torture and trauma, particularly refugees and immigrants. Providing mental health counseling, case management, and supportive services to help survivors heal and rebuild their lives.
eligibility: Survivors of torture, refugees, and immigrants experiencing trauma

name: Community Action Partnership - Neighborhood Assistance
description: Anti-poverty organization providing utility assistance, weatherization, energy conservation programs, and other services to help low-income families achieve self-sufficiency. LIHEAP applications and emergency utility help available.
eligibility: Low-income households meeting federal poverty guidelines

name: Home of the Innocents
description: Comprehensive pediatric healthcare and child services organization providing specialized medical care, foster care, adoption services, therapy, and support for children with complex needs and their families.
eligibility: Children with medical complexities, foster care needs, or requiring specialized support.

name: Center for Accessible Living
description: Independent living center providing advocacy, support services, and resources for people with disabilities. Helping individuals live independently in the community with peer support, skills training, and advocacy.
eligibility: Individuals with disabilities of all ages

name: YMCA of Greater Louisville - Main Office
description: Community organization offering childcare, youth programs, fitness, and family services at multiple locations throughout Louisville. Before and after school care, summer camps, swimming lessons, and more.
hours: Varies by location, typically Mon-Fri 5:30AM-9PM, Sat-Sun 7AM-6PM
eligibility: Open to all. Financial assistance available.

name: Boys & Girls Clubs of Kentuckiana
description: Youth development organization providing after-school programs, mentoring, academic support, and recreational activities for children and teens. Multiple club locations throughout Louisville.
hours: Mon-Fri 3PM-7PM during school year, extended summer hours
eligibility: Youth ages 6-18. Membership fees apply, scholarships available.

name: Louisville Community Grocery
description: Nonprofit grocery store offering fresh, affordable food to residents in food deserts. Pay-what-you-can model ensuring everyone has access to healthy food regardless of income. Located in West Louisville.
eligibility: Open to all, especially West Louisville residents

name: The Healing Place
description: Recovery program for men and women struggling with addiction and homelessness. Providing shelter, addiction recovery services, job training, and supportive housing in a Christ-centered environment. Separate men's and women's facilities.
eligibility: Adults struggling with addiction and/or homelessness. Must be willing to participate in recovery program.

name: Jeffersontown Area Ministries
description: Faith-based community ministry serving Jeffersontown and surrounding East Louisville areas. Providing emergency assistance with food, utilities, rent, and connection to community resources.
eligibility: Jeffersontown area residents. Call for appointment.

name: Louisville Metro Adult Education
description: Free adult education services for Louisville residents including GED preparation, high school equivalency, English as a Second Language (ESL), and basic literacy skills. Classes at multiple locations throughout the city.
eligibility: Adults 18+ not enrolled in high school

name: Dress for Success Louisville
description: Nonprofit empowering women to achieve economic independence by providing professional attire, career development tools, and network support. Free professional clothing and career services for job-seeking women.
eligibility: Women seeking employment or career advancement. Referral from partner agency or direct call.

name: Family Health Centers - Fairdale
description: Community health center serving Southwest Louisville and Fairdale area. Comprehensive primary care, dental, and behavioral health services with sliding scale fees available.
eligibility: All patients welcome. Sliding fee scale based on income.

name: Norton Women's & Children's Hospital
description: Specialized hospital providing comprehensive women's health services, maternity care, NICU, pediatric emergency services, and children's specialty care. Part of Norton Healthcare network.
eligibility: All patients. Financial assistance available.

name: EmployAbility
description: Employment services for people with disabilities and disadvantages. Providing job training, placement, supported employment, and career development services throughout Louisville.
eligibility: Individuals with disabilities or barriers to employment

name: Newburg Community Center
description: Community center in Southeast Louisville providing recreational programs, meeting space, computer access, and community events. Free WiFi available. Serves the Newburg neighborhood and surrounding areas.
eligibility: Open to all community members

name: Neighborhood Place - Bridges of Hope
description: One-stop center for Metro social services offering assistance with food stamps (SNAP), Medicaid, child care assistance, WIC, and connections to community resources. Walk-in services available.
eligibility: Open to all residents. Income guidelines apply for specific benefits.

name: Neighborhood Place - South Central
description: Multi-service center providing access to public assistance programs including food stamps, Medicaid, child care assistance, and community referrals. Serving South Louisville neighborhoods.
eligibility: Open to all Louisville residents. Income-based programs available.

name: Americana Community Center
description: Multicultural community center serving immigrant and refugee families in South Louisville. Providing ESL classes, citizenship assistance, job training, youth programs, and community support services.
eligibility: Open to all, with focus on immigrant and refugee communities.

name: Coalition for the Homeless - Resource Center
description: Coordinating organization for homeless services in Louisville. Provides shelter access coordination, homeless prevention, rapid rehousing assistance, and connections to all homeless service providers in the area.
eligibility: Individuals and families experiencing or at risk of homelessness.

name: Volunteers of America Mid-States
description: Comprehensive human services organization providing affordable housing, veteran services, substance abuse recovery programs, and supportive services. Operating multiple housing sites and programs throughout Louisville.
eligibility: Varies by program. Housing programs for low-income families, veterans, and seniors.

name: Catholic Charities - Father Jack Jones Food Pantry
description: Client-choice food pantry serving South Louisville with groceries and household items. Part of Catholic Charities network providing dignity-centered food assistance where clients select their own food items.
eligibility: South Louisville residents. Photo ID required.

name: Catholic Charities - Sister Visitor Center
description: West Louisville food pantry and community resource center serving families in need. Choice-model food pantry allowing clients to select their own groceries, plus emergency assistance and support services.
eligibility: West Louisville residents. Call for appointment.

name: St. Matthews Area Ministries
description: Community ministry serving East Louisville including St. Matthews, Lyndon, and Middletown areas. Providing emergency assistance with food, utilities, rent, and other basic needs plus case management services.
eligibility: East Louisville residents including St. Matthews, Lyndon, Middletown areas.

name: Family Health Centers - East Broadway
description: Community health center in East Louisville providing comprehensive primary care, dental, behavioral health, and pharmacy services. We accept all patients regardless of ability to pay and offer sliding scale fees based on income.
eligibility: All patients welcome. Sliding fee scale available.

name: Phoenix Health Center - Care for the Homeless
description: Health center providing medical, dental, and behavioral health services specifically for individuals experiencing homelessness. No insurance required, no ID needed. Walk-ins welcome. Part of Family Health Centers network.
eligibility: Open to all, especially those experiencing homelessness. No insurance or ID required.

name: South Louisville Community Ministries
description: Faith-based community organization providing emergency food assistance, financial assistance for utilities and rent, clothing, and case management. Serving South Louisville neighborhoods including Beechmont, Iroquois, and Okolona areas.
eligibility: South Louisville residents. Photo ID and proof of address required.

name: Shively Area Ministries
description: Community ministry serving Shively and West Louisville with emergency food assistance, utility help, and support services. We provide groceries, hot meals, and connection to other community resources.
eligibility: Shively and West Louisville residents in need. Call for appointment.

name: Highlands Community Ministries
description: Comprehensive community organization serving the Highlands and surrounding neighborhoods. Offering food assistance, child care, senior services, and community programs. Multiple locations throughout East Louisville.
hours: Mon-Fri 9AM-4PM, Food Pantry Wed-Thu by appointment
eligibility: Varies by program. Most services available to East Louisville residents.

name: St. Vincent de Paul - Food Pantry
description: Community food pantry providing groceries and household items to families in need. We offer emergency food assistance through our client choice pantry model, allowing families to select foods that meet their cultural and dietary needs. Open to Jefferson County residents.
eligibility: Jefferson County residents in need. Photo ID and proof of address required.

name: Salvation Army - Center of Hope
description: Food pantry and community center providing emergency food assistance, meals, and social services. We offer food boxes, kids' cafe, and various support programs for individuals and families in need. Food box pickup available by reservation.
hours: Tue 1PM for food box pickup (call to reserve)
eligibility: Low-income individuals and families in Louisville area.

name: Louisville Free Public Library - Main Branch
description: Free public library offering books, computers, internet access, educational programs, and learning resources. We provide technology training, homework help, adult literacy programs, job search assistance, and community meeting spaces. Library card is free for all Kentucky residents.
eligibility: Free library card for all Kentucky residents. Guest passes available for non-residents.

name: Jefferson Community and Technical College
description: Community college offering affordable associate degrees, technical certificates, and workforce training programs. We provide financial aid, career counseling, and support services to help students succeed. Multiple campus locations serving Louisville and surrounding counties.
eligibility: Open enrollment. High school diploma or GED required for most programs. Adult education available.

name: Family and Children's Place
description: Comprehensive family support organization providing childcare assistance, parenting classes, family counseling, and resource navigation. We help families access the services they need to thrive. Our child care assistance program helps low-income families afford quality childcare.
eligibility: Varies by program. Childcare assistance based on income. Family support services open to all.

name: LG&E and KU - Customer Service
description: Electric and gas utility company serving Louisville and Kentucky. We offer payment assistance programs, budget billing, and energy efficiency programs to help customers manage utility costs. LIHEAP and other assistance programs available for eligible customers.
eligibility: Must be LG&E/KU customer. Income-based assistance programs available.

name: Goodwill West Louisville Opportunity Center
description: Goodwill Kentucky has become a vital part of a community that has endured years of disinvestment. The organization strives to which provide a collection of resources to individuals looking to escape poverty.
eligibility: Open to all job seekers

name: Park DuValle Community Health Center
description: Full-service community health center providing comprehensive primary care, pediatrics, dental services, behavioral health, and pharmacy services. We offer sliding scale fees and accept most insurance including Medicaid and Medicare. No one is turned away due to inability to pay.
eligibility: Open to all patients. Sliding fee scale available based on income.

name: Dare to Care Food Bank
description: Kentuckiana's largest food bank serving 13 counties. We distribute food through partner agencies, mobile pantries, and direct services. Fighting hunger and food insecurity by providing nutritious food to individuals and families in need. We serve over 200,000 people annually.
eligibility: Individuals and families experiencing food insecurity. No income verification required for emergency assistance.

name: Louisville Urban League - Employment Services
description: Comprehensive employment services helping connect job seekers with meaningful career opportunities. We provide job training, resume assistance, interview preparation, professional development workshops, and direct connections to employers. Our programs focus on economic empowerment and removing barriers to employment.
eligibility: Open to all job seekers. Priority given to underserved populations.

name: Norton Hospital - Emergency Department
description: Full-service hospital with 24/7 emergency department providing comprehensive medical services including emergency care, trauma services, specialized treatments, and inpatient care. Part of Norton Healthcare system serving Louisville and surrounding areas.
eligibility: Open to all patients. Financial assistance available for uninsured/underinsured.

name: Family Health Centers - Portland
description: Community health center providing medical, dental, and behavioral health services. We offer comprehensive primary care with sliding scale fees based on income. Same-day appointments available for urgent needs.
eligibility: All patients welcome. Sliding fee scale available.

name: Family Health Centers - Iroquois
description: Neighborhood health center serving South Louisville with primary care, pediatrics, dental services, and behavioral health. We provide affordable healthcare with sliding scale fees and accept most insurance.
eligibility: Open to all. Sliding fee scale based on income.

name: Wayside Christian Mission
description: Emergency shelter and comprehensive services for people experiencing homelessness. We provide safe shelter, meals, case management, job training, addiction recovery programs, and permanent housing assistance. Our goal is to help individuals and families achieve self-sufficiency.
eligibility: Open to all individuals and families experiencing homelessness.

name: Legal Aid Society
description: Free legal services for low-income individuals and families in civil legal matters. We provide representation, advice, and self-help resources in housing, family law, public benefits, consumer issues, and more. No criminal defense provided.
eligibility: Must meet income guidelines (typically 125% of federal poverty level).

name: Center for Women and Families
description: Comprehensive services for survivors of domestic violence and sexual assault. We provide emergency shelter, 24/7 crisis hotline, counseling, legal advocacy, and support groups. All services are free and confidential. Crisis hotline available 24/7.
eligibility: Services available to all survivors of domestic violence and sexual assault.

name: Seven Counties Services - Crisis Center
description: Mental health and substance abuse crisis services including 24/7 crisis line, walk-in assessments, mobile crisis teams, and emergency psychiatric care. We provide immediate support for individuals experiencing mental health or addiction crises.
eligibility: Open to all individuals experiencing mental health or substance abuse crisis.

name: Louisville Metro Housing Authority
description: Provides affordable housing assistance through public housing and Housing Choice Vouchers (Section 8). We help Louisville residents find and maintain safe, affordable housing for low-income families, elderly, and persons with disabilities.
eligibility: Income limits apply (typically 50-80% of area median income). Must be US citizen or eligible immigrant.

name: Kentucky Career Center - Broadway
description: One-stop career center offering free employment services including job search assistance, skills training, career counseling, and employer connections. Part of KentuckianaWorks serving Louisville job seekers at all levels.
eligibility: Open to all job seekers, unemployed workers, and career changers.
